LESSON: MODERN SLAVERY AND SERVITUDE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: International Themes
Topic 3.3: Modern Slavery and Servitude
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Modern Slavery and Servitude, part of International Themes in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can you end slavery and servitude in the world?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discuss various forms of slavery and servitude in the modern world,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modern Slavery and Servitude in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modern Slavery and Servitude in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Modern Slavery and Servitude together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem solving: the skill of Interpretation and inference as learners research on possible solutions to

end slavery and servitude.

55

● Self-Efficacy: Skill of effective communication skills as learner writes an essay on possible solutions to end slavery and

servitude.

Values:
● Social Justice: Skills of upholding human dignity as the learner appreciates the need to end slavery and servitude.

● Love: skills of empathy and compassion as the learner identifies ways in which governments and civil society collaborate

to end various forms of slavery and servitude in the society today.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social awareness skills: as the learner composes a song/poem and sings/recites on possible solutions to end slavery and

servitude and sing in school.

Key skills

● Discussing various forms of slavery and servitude in the modern world.

● Illustrating ways in which governments and civil society collaborate to end various forms of slavery and servitude in the

society.

● Assessing the factors that cause slavery and servitude in the modern world.

Suggested learning resources

Digital devices with assistive technology, Printed media, Braille machine, Braille paper, slate and stylus, Approved braille and

print textbooks, Adaptive keyboard, Orbit Readers, Resource person..
